background: NWB Bank is the Dutch water boards' bank, owned by the water authorities, the Dutch state and the provinces, which lends to Dutch public-sector bodies, housing associations and healthcare providers and funds itself in the bond markets.
synthesis: The bank is rated AAA on average across two of the three main agencies, both at the top of the scale on a stable outlook, with the last move a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 24 Nov 2015. The ratios are far outside the range of ordinary banks: CET1 of 36.8% and leverage of 39.2% are both in the top quarter of EU and Nordic peers, as are LCR of 243% and NSFR of 148%. Leverage has risen 30.6 points since 30 Jun 2023, a jump that size being more likely a change in how the ratio is calculated than in the bank itself, while CET1 has fallen 1.1 points; the figures run to 31 Dec 2025. Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days: a public-sector lender with sovereign-level ratings.
